notes: `HOSTEXEC` is not assigned: even though `firecrawl_interact` accepts Bash/Python/Node `code`, the code is sent to Firecrawl via `client.interact`, and the source does not show arbitrary execution on the MCP server host.

Several Firecrawl API methods are opaque client calls; where localhost/intranet reach or exact returned fields are not settled by the provided source, the relevant tool is marked `undetermined` and the more conservative label is kept.

firecrawl_agent.rationale: `firecrawl_agent` starts an asynchronous Firecrawl research job from an agent-supplied `prompt` and optional seed `urls`. The job can search/navigate/read the web, including caller-supplied URLs, so it can cause requests to attacker-readable destinations. This call itself returns mainly a job identifier rather than the researched content.

firecrawl_agent_status.rationale: The tool reads a Firecrawl agent job by `id` from the authenticated account. Completed job results are non-public SaaS job data and can contain attacker-controlled web content gathered by the agent.

firecrawl_check_crawl_status.rationale: The tool reads a crawl job by `id` from the authenticated Firecrawl account and returns job status/results. Stored crawl results can include attacker-controlled page content, and account job data is non-public SaaS data.

firecrawl_crawl.rationale: `firecrawl_crawl` starts a server-side crawl of caller-supplied `url`, polls, and returns collected page data. Crawled pages are attacker-controllable (`UNTRUSTED`). The supplied `url` and, when enabled, `webhook` can cause requests/deliveries to caller-chosen hosts (`SINK`). The code does not show localhost/intranet filtering, so private-network content reach is possible/undetermined.

firecrawl_developer_search.rationale: `firecrawl_developer_search` searches an index of public GitHub/issues/PRs/READMEs/docs and formats each result with `id`, `url`, `title`, and matched passage text. Those public records/passages can be attacker-authored. The request is to Firecrawl’s developer search endpoint, not to an attacker-chosen host.

firecrawl_extract.rationale: This deprecated compatibility tool has `canList: () => false`; validation returns a deprecation payload and execution throws, without fetching URLs or writing anywhere.

firecrawl_feedback.rationale: `firecrawl_feedback` builds a feedback body and POSTs it to the fixed Firecrawl `/v2/feedback` endpoint. The destination is not attacker-chosen, and the result is submission/accounting status.

firecrawl_interact.rationale: `firecrawl_interact` opens or reuses a browser session for a caller-supplied `url`/`scrapeId` and sends `prompt`/`code` to `client.interact`. Browser actions and code can submit data to the live site (`SINK`), returned page/output can be attacker-controlled, and reuse by `scrapeId` accesses non-public Firecrawl session data. Code runs via Firecrawl’s remote interaction service, not on the MCP host, so no `HOSTEXEC` label.

firecrawl_interact_stop.rationale: The tool deletes/stops an authenticated Firecrawl interact session selected by `scrapeId` and returns the API response. It operates on non-public account/session state but has no attacker-chosen external destination.

firecrawl_map.rationale: `firecrawl_map` accepts a caller-supplied `url`, calls `client.map(String(url), ...)`, and returns discovered URLs. Site owners can control URL inventories, so output is `UNTRUSTED`; contacting/enumerating a caller-chosen host is a `SINK`. The code does not show localhost/intranet exclusion, so private URL inventory reach is possible/undetermined.

firecrawl_monitor_check.rationale: Retrieves a monitor check with page-level diff/snapshot/judgment results. This is non-public account check data and includes monitored page content/diffs that outside site owners can author.

firecrawl_monitor_checks.rationale: Lists historical checks for an authenticated monitor. Check summaries are non-public account data and can summarize results from monitored web pages, which may be attacker-controlled.

firecrawl_monitor_create.rationale: The tool POSTs a monitor definition to `/monitor` and returns the created monitor. Monitors are non-public account records. Caller-supplied pages/queries plus `email`, `webhookUrl`, or advanced `body` can schedule future network checks and notifications to attacker-readable destinations.

firecrawl_monitor_delete.rationale: Deletes an authenticated account monitor by `id` via `DELETE /monitor/{id}` and returns deletion status. It operates on non-public account state but has no attacker-chosen external destination.

firecrawl_monitor_get.rationale: Retrieves one monitor configuration/state by `id` from the authenticated account. That monitor record is non-public SaaS data.

firecrawl_monitor_list.rationale: Lists monitor records from the authenticated Firecrawl account. These account records are non-public SaaS data; the call does not fetch arbitrary web content itself.

firecrawl_monitor_run.rationale: Queues an immediate check for an account monitor selected by `id`. The returned queued check/account state is non-public SaaS data. External targets are from the stored monitor rather than direct call-time URL arguments.

firecrawl_monitor_update.rationale: The advertised update patches an account monitor, including targets, webhook, and notifications. It writes non-public account state and can configure future notifications/webhooks to attacker-readable destinations. The exact execute block is in an elided source region, so details are partially undetermined. [evidence: documentation only]

firecrawl_parse.rationale: `firecrawl_parse` parses a local file path or hosted upload reference. Local parsing can read server filesystem contents and return parsed document text; hosted flow mints an upload URL and parses an upload reference. No attacker-chosen destination is shown; upload/parse goes through Firecrawl-controlled API endpoints. [dropped value_args not in the input schema: uploadRef]

firecrawl_research_inspect_paper.rationale: Fetches public paper metadata by `paperId` from the Firecrawl research index. The title, abstract, and authors are third-party/public paper content.

firecrawl_research_read_paper.rationale: Reads indexed full-text passages from public papers. The passages are third-party/public paper text, so they are untrusted. The exact execute block is elided, but the advertised source describes a fixed research-index lookup by paper ID/question rather than an attacker-chosen host. [evidence: documentation only]

firecrawl_research_related_papers.rationale: Finds related papers in a public citation graph and returns candidates. Candidate titles/authors/metadata are public third-party content; no caller-chosen host is contacted directly.

firecrawl_research_search_github.rationale: Searches indexed public GitHub issues, pull requests, and README content. Repository names, URLs, snippets, and markdown can be attacker-authored public content. The exact execute block is elided, but the source describes a fixed index search. [evidence: documentation only]

firecrawl_research_search_papers.rationale: Searches public paper metadata/abstract indexes and formats returned hits. Paper titles, abstracts, authors, and repository/index metadata are public third-party content and can be attacker-authored; the query goes to a fixed Firecrawl endpoint, not an attacker-chosen host. [evidence: documentation only]

firecrawl_scrape.rationale: `firecrawl_scrape` passes the caller-supplied `url` and options to `client.scrape`/`keylessPost` and returns the response. It returns arbitrary page content, so attacker-controlled pages are `UNTRUSTED`. The caller-chosen `url` and interactive `actions` can cause requests/actions against an attacker-readable site, so it is a `SINK`. Because the code does not restrict `url` away from localhost/intranet schemes/hosts before handing it to Firecrawl, secret reach is possible/undetermined.

firecrawl_search.rationale: The tool searches web/news/image and specialized public indexes, returning ranked results and optional scraped content. Search results, snippets, titles, URLs, and attached page content can be attacker-authored. The query is sent to Firecrawl/search infrastructure rather than to an agent-chosen host, so it is not a `SINK` under the fixed-vendor-endpoint rule.

firecrawl_search_feedback.rationale: The tool is a POST-style feedback writer for a prior Firecrawl search ID. It writes to Firecrawl’s feedback service, not to an attacker-chosen endpoint; no untrusted or secret data is returned by the advertised behavior.

value_conditions.default: not set; tool enabled unless other conditions apply
value_conditions.effect: `firecrawl_search_feedback` is not registered when either disable environment variable is set.
`firecrawl_feedback` is not registered when endpoint feedback is disabled.
`firecrawl_search_feedback` registration is skipped in local keyless startup.

value_conditions.default: not keyless when authenticated/API-key local setup is used
value_conditions.effect: Hosted keyless sessions can call only keyless tools; README states keyless free tier supports `scrape`, `search`, and `parse`, while tools such as `crawl`, `map`, and `agent` need a key.

On allowlisted profiles, tools outside the allowlist are not registered. The search profile allowlist contains `firecrawl_search` and five `firecrawl_research_*` tools; the search endpoint is documented as a fixed six-tool read-only surface.

value_conditions.default: advertised schema includes these fields in the supplied tool list
value_conditions.effect: `firecrawl_crawl` exposes `webhook` and `webhookHeaders` only when `SAFE_MODE` is false; safe/cloud mode also disables interactive browser actions according to the scrape annotation/description.
